title: Routing
description: What the resolver, failover and consent read beside the presets (F2 D1.2): link classes, task tiers, drivers, exempt and card roles, the roles the workflow requires, failover timing, consent, card facts and the credentials backend. Owner-only: only the owner's path writes it.

class.description: The id of a link class (link_classes[]).

class_order.description: Link classes in the order they are tried, at least one (an empty order would leave the role no link). An item is a class id, or a list of class ids: the best suited of these. `check` refuses an id link_classes does not define.

privacy_rank.description: 0 is the most private; a move to a class with a higher rank is a move to a less private class (the owner is notified).

hosted.description: Whether links of this class leave the machine. `check` refuses a class with hosted false on a link whose reach is not local (stella_data.reach(): cloud, a hosted connection, an aggregator); the locality rules themselves read reach(), never this label.

local.description: The class of a link that names none and whose reach is local.

aggregator.description: The class of an aggregator's link that names none.

class_defaults.description: The class of a link whose connection and model name no link_class (stella_data.link_class()). Any other link without a class is not routable.

task_tiers.description: The task tiers a preset's frontier_when may list (the planner rubric's project tiers).

mid_task.description: Whether a link driven this way may switch mid-task (the engine's own model loop) or only between attempts (a worker CLI). A cli-login connection never switches mid-task, whatever the driver.

role.description: A role of the role table.

in_fallback_chain.description: False: the role has no fallback chain (its own class order only, no failover to another link).

exempt_roles.description: Roles the preset class rules do not apply to: each follows its own class order under every preset, and that is never a last-resort crossing. `check` refuses a class order here that names a hosted class: no preset's localities bind these roles, so the order itself keeps them on links that do not leave the machine.

card_roles.description: The roles that work a card: the resolver refuses one of them with no card (the card facts decide the hard exclusions).

when.description: `always`, or the id of a trigger (triggers{}): the role is required while that trigger can fire.

required_roles.description: The roles the workflow requires: `check` refuses a preset that sets one inactive.

scope.description: What the cooldown covers: the one link (connection plus model), or every link of the connection.

triggers.description: The failures that move a task to the next link, by id: exactly the trigger ids a protocol's errors[] may name (the enum of the protocols schema), every one present, so no failure a protocol reports is left without a way on. Each with its cooldown: until = now + cooldown_s, doubled per repeated failure up to max_cooldown_s.

same_connection_first.description: True: the next model of the same connection is tried before the task leaves that connection.

retry_count.description: How often the same link is tried again before the switch.

approval_class.description: The approval class of a consent request (an approval_class of the approval-request schema).

alert_code_queue.description: The alert of a task queued for a grant (unattended mode on): a code of the alert catalog.

alert_code_notice.description: The alert of a move to a less private link class: a code of the alert catalog.

builder_roles.description: The card roles that build (the QA loop's builder escalation applies to them only): each built-in preset ships an escalation_chain for every one. `check` refuses a role that is not a card role (card_roles).

purposes.description: {purpose: role} (owner decision 2026-11-18, F2b item E): whose escalation chain bin/escalate.sh walks for a call of that purpose (the card's current rung of that role, state/rungs.json, default 1). A purpose with no row is refused (STL-MDL-747). `check` refuses a role that is not an assignable role of the role table.

escalation.description: The escalation calls of bin/escalate.sh. Absent: no purpose has a row, so every call is refused.

levels.description: The effort ids (a reasoning effort or thinking setting), lowest first: the only ids a link's parameters.effort and by_role may name (`check` refuses any other, here and in every link of the role assignments).

tiers.description: Per task tier (task_tiers[]): the role's effort at that tier.

by_role.description: Per role of the role table: an effort id (the role's default), or {default, tiers}: its effort by task tier, else its default (the id form keeps a table of many roles a reference to the role table, not a copy of it, for the one-owner lint). `check` refuses a role, a tier or an effort id the data does not define.

effort.description: Effort as data (F2b B3): every link the resolver answers carries `effort`: its parameters.effort when set, else by_role[role].tiers[tier], else by_role[role].default, else null. Absent: no effort id exists, so a link that names one is refused.

when_missing.description: The card facts the resolver judges (the fields of a facts record that exclude every hosted link while they hold): carries_secrets and vault_content always, and any fact added here. The value is what a missing record or a missing field counts as, and it is always true: a fact that is not recorded holds (fail closed), and no setting turns a hard exclusion off.

card_facts.description: The card facts are a host-side store (index key card_facts: one <card>.json per card, written on the host only), never the card document an agent writes.

backend.description: The backend in use: a key of backends.

kind.description: none: every read is refused with a code (until the secrets broker, B1). dir: one file per name in a folder (a test backend).

path.description: kind dir: the folder, relative to the stack root; `check` refuses one that is not inside a protected state path of the index.

probe.description: The capability probe's settings (bin/probe.py): the token lengths of the context test (the probe runs them ascending), the chains planted at each (`needles` chains of `hops` hops: each hop is a code that the next code is looked up from), the share of the shortest length's score a longer length may lose and still count (`tolerance`), the output shapes strongest first (the ids a wire shape's request.output_shape names a pointer for, then none), how often a shape is tried before it counts as proved (`shape_trials`), and the repair retries of the structured-output helper.
